title: IPv6-transition SSRF tests must use a real encoding of the embedded IPv4
answers: how to write a test for IPv6 6to4 SSRF handling
test for NAT64 webhook blocking passes even without the fix
which IPv6 address to use in webhook SSRF tests
mock assertion rule for SSRF validation tests
body:
Convention: Test cases for transition-address handling use an address that `ipaddress` actually decodes, e.g. 6to4 `2002:a9fe:a9fe::` for 169.254.169.254 (`.sixtofour` returns it), not a documentation-prefix address such as 2001:db8::/32.
Why: documentation-prefix addresses are already non-public and have `sixtofour=None`, so the test passes even if the decoding branch is removed (raised in review and verified load-bearing in 295d1e0).
Mocks: each `mock.patch` in these tests (`socket.getaddrinfo`, `socket.socket.getpeername`) is captured and asserted called, per the repo's mock-assertion rule.
Positive cases such as `::ffff:8.8.8.8` and `2001:4860:4860::8888` belong alongside the blocked cases so the test fails on over-blocking too.
applies: Tests for webhook URL validation and the connection-time SSRF guard.
says: Outgoing webhooks reach internal cloud metadata endpoints when using IPv6 transition formats.
Webhook endpoint validation should block embedded private network addresses disguised in IPv6.
Webhook delivery security fails to catch internal server destinations wrapped in transition formats.
Valid public IPv6 webhook destinations are incorrectly rejected by outgoing security checks.
search: Tests for webhook URL validation and connection-time SSRF guards handling IPv6 transition addresses must use real decodable addresses such as 6to4 2002:a9fe:a9fe:: for 169.254.169.254 rather than documentation-prefix addresses like 2001:db8::/32. Documentation prefixes already count as non-public with sixtofour returning None, allowing tests to pass even if decoding branches are removed. Per repo mock-assertion rules, every mock.patch on socket.getaddrinfo and socket.socket.getpeername must be captured and asserted called. Positive cases including ::ffff:8.8.8.8 and 2001:4860:4860::8888 must be included alongside blocked cases to detect over-blocking in tests/utils/test_validation.py and tests/webhooks/test_ssrf.py.
